trial_court: III Additional District Munsif's Court, Vijayawada, O.S. No. 776 of 1989
case_name: Vajji Venkataramesh vs Vajji Padmalatha Styled As Gutts
facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent got married on June 21, 1988, but the respondent filed a petition under Section 12 (1) (c) of the Hindu Marriage Act seeking annulment of marriage due to force and fraud. The petitioner filed a suit for permanent injunction restraining the respondent from marrying another person.

legal_principles.principle: There can be no legal bar for simultaneous proceedings being taken, yet there may be cases where it would be appropriate to defer disciplinary proceedings awaiting disposal of the criminal case.
legal_principles.held: It was held that there can be no legal bar for simultaneous proceedings being taken, yet there may be cases where it would be appropriate to defer disciplinary proceedings awaiting disposal of the criminal case.
cited_cases: Kusheshwar Dubey v. Bharat Coking Coal Ltd., (1988) 4 S C C 319

legal_principles.principle: The doctrine of estoppel is based on the principle that consistency in word and action imparts certainty and honesty to human affairs.
legal_principles.held: The doctrine of estoppel is based on the principle that consistency in word and action imparts certainty and honesty to human affairs.

legal_principles.principle: Fundamental rights are undoubtedly conferred by the Constitution upon individuals which have to be asserted and enforced by them if those rights are violated.
legal_principles.held: Fundamental rights are undoubtedly conferred by the Constitution upon individuals which have to be asserted and enforced by them if those rights are violated.
cited_cases: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation,

legal_principles.principle: There can be no waiver of the fundamental rights founded on Article 14 of the Constitution.
legal_principles.held: It is true if it is a case arising out of violation of fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 20(3) of the Constitution that there can be no waiver of the fundamental rights founded on Article 14 of the Constitution.
cited_cases: Basheshwar Nath v. Commissioner of Income-Tax, Delhi, (1959)

outcome.final_order: The learned Subordinate Judge found that the civil proceedings have reached the stage of trial and the criminal proceedings are still at the committal stage before the Magistrates, and hence dismissed the application.
